h1:
Koh Phangan Wellness
Yoga, Vegan Cafes, Spa & Sunsets in 3 Days
intro: Koh Phangan isn't just the Full Moon Party. The other side of the island, an area called Sri Thanu, is the wellness pocket where people fly in from all over the world to stay for weeks — doing yoga, eating clean, getting massages, then sitting on the beach to watch the sunset. This plan keeps things slow across 3 days and 2 nights, all about resting your body and mind, with short travel times since everything clusters on the island's west side. Real spots, real ballpark prices, places that are open right now.

blocks.html: If the name Koh Phangan only makes you think of the Haad Rin party scene, take a look at the other side of the island. The west coast around Sri Thanu–Hin Kong is a wellness community that has slowly grown since around 2005. Today you'll find yoga studios, healing centers, vegan restaurants, massage shops, and sunset beaches all within a few kilometers of each other. One rented motorbike covers the whole area. So this plan keeps things unhurried: wake up for yoga, eat a clean meal, get a massage in the afternoon, then close the day with a sunset.

Sri Thanu sits on the west of the island, about 10–15 minutes from Thong Sala pier by motorbike. The appeal here is that everything is walkable or a short ride away. If you eat vegan or have food allergies, almost every spot clearly labels its dishes vegan / raw / gluten-free, so finding something to eat is far easier than anywhere else on the island. It suits people who actually want to rest, not chase the party.

items: Yoga — big studios like Orion Healing and Samma Karuna sit right on the beach, with drop-in classes so you don't have to sign up for a long course
Clean food — vegan cafes line the main Sri Thanu road and the Hin Kong sunset road
Massage & spa — good massage shops start in the low hundreds of baht, from Thai massage to full spa treatments
Sunsets — Zen Beach in the middle of Sri Thanu, plus the hilltop Amsterdam Bar at Wok Tum, less than 15 minutes apart

blocks.title: An honest note on accommodation
blocks.html: Room prices on Koh Phangan swing hard with the seasons, especially nights near the Full Moon Party, when prices double and rooms fill fast. If you're here for wellness and want it quiet, avoid Full Moon week, book ahead, and choose a place on the Sri Thanu–Hin Kong side, which is well away from the Haad Rin party noise.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrive, settle in, start at Zen Beach

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Arrive, check in at Sri Thanu, first sunset

items.activity: Get off the boat at Thong Sala, rent a motorbike, and ride over to check in on the Sri Thanu side
items.note: The island roads have several steep hills. If you're not used to riding, go slow, wear a helmet, and avoid riding at night after rain when the roads get slippery.

items.activity: Settle in at your place, unpack, drink some water, and recover from the journey
items.note: Don't pack in activities yet — ease into the rhythm on day one.

items.activity: Ride over and park near Sri Thanu, walk down to Zen Beach, and find a spot by the water
items.note: Zen Beach sits in the middle of the Sri Thanu area — white sand, clear water, and one of the island's most popular sunset spots.

items.activity: Watch the sunset. There's an informal live drum circle that starts around 17:30 and goes until dark
items.note: The vibe is chill — people doing fire shows, music, and acro-yoga on the sand. You can drink, but drink responsibly and keep an eye on your bag and valuables.

items.activity: Vegan dinner around Sri Thanu — try Karma Kafe, with lots of plants and chill music
items.note: Sri Thanu makes finding vegan spots easy; you can walk between several options in the same area.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Morning yoga, clean cafes, afternoon massage, hillside sunset

items.activity: Morning drop-in yoga class at Orion Healing or Samma Karuna, right by Sri Thanu–Chao Phao beach
items.note: Drop-in classes run roughly 300–400 THB (Orion) and 250–350 THB (Samma Karuna). You can book or just walk in and check the schedule on the spot — no long course required.

items.activity: Post-yoga breakfast at Eat.Co (Eat Consciously), the vegan spot people talk about most on the island
items.note: A wide menu with standout desserts; prices lean a little premium. The main branch is in Sri Thanu, with a brunch cafe in Thong Sala.

items.activity: Let it digest — wander around Sri Thanu and pop into the local shops, bookstores, and crystal shops
items.note: The late-morning sun gets strong, so put on sunscreen and carry water.

items.activity: Lunch at Street Vegan, a Vietnamese-style vegan street food spot around Hin Kong
items.note: Open Monday–Saturday, roughly 13:00–22:00, right on the main road. Ride over or grab a songthaew.

items.activity: A relaxing massage at Pure Relax Spa (Sri Thanu branch) or Revive Massage
items.note: Pure Relax's Sri Thanu branch has private massage rooms; Thai massage starts around 400 THB/hour, with oil, hot stone, and body scrub options, open until midnight. · Revive is known for therapists who find the right pressure points and plays mantra music instead of the usual spa tracks.

items.activity: Ride to Amsterdam Bar at Wok Tum, a hilltop bar with panoramic sunset views
items.note: About 10 minutes from Thong Sala. Get there by ~16:30 to grab a good seat. There's an entry fee or minimum drink spend of around 100–200 THB. Open 12:00–01:00; the sunset is best around 17:30–18:30.

items.activity: Dinner at Pure Vegan Heaven on the Hin Kong sunset road, or head back to eat around Sri Thanu
items.note: The menu covers burgers, bowls, and burritos, all made fresh, in a spot right on the sunset road.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Closing yoga, a slow meal before the boat

items.activity: A gentle yoga or breathwork class to close out the trip
items.note: If you're tired from the day before, choose an easy stretch class instead of a hard one.

items.activity: One last slow meal at a health cafe in the area — order a smoothie bowl or coffee
items.note: Leave time to return the bike, hand back your keys, and check the boat schedule ahead.

items.activity: Return the motorbike, pack up, and ride to Thong Sala pier
items.note: Allow at least 30–45 minutes to reach the pier before the boat leaves, especially on busy days.

items.activity: Take the boat back to the mainland (Surat Thani / Koh Samui / Koh Tao, depending on your plan)
items.note: Seas can be rough during monsoon season, so bring seasickness pills if you're prone to it.

blocks.text: Health cafes and vegan spots worth trying

items.name: Eat.Co (Eat Consciously)
items.blurb: The most talked-about vegan spot on Koh Phangan. Carefully made food with standout desserts and a varied menu — great for a post-yoga breakfast or a long brunch.
items.meta: Sri Thanu (main branch) + Thong Sala · prices lean premium

items.name: Street Vegan
items.blurb: Vietnamese-style vegan street food at friendly prices — perfect for a quick lunch mid-day.
items.meta: Hin Kong, on the main road · open Mon–Sat ~13:00–22:00

items.name: Pure Vegan Heaven
items.blurb: Moved to a new spot on the Hin Kong sunset road. Hearty plates — burgers, bowls, burritos — made fresh and filling.

items.name: Karma Kafe
items.blurb: A Bali-feel cafe with lots of plants and chill music. Mostly vegetarian with vegan options — good for a long, lingering dinner.

blocks.html: All four are within the Sri Thanu–Hin Kong radius, just minutes apart by bike. If you only have time for one meal, Eat.Co is where most people stop. But if you want something easy and light on the wallet, Street Vegan does the job well.

blocks.text: Massage and spa in the area

items.name: Pure Relax Spa, Sri Thanu branch
items.blurb: Private massage rooms in the middle of Sri Thanu. Thai massage starts around 400 THB/hour, with oil, hot stone, body scrub, and herbal compress options, open late until midnight.

items.name: Revive Massage
items.blurb: Known for therapists who find the right pressure points and understand anatomy, with mantra music instead of typical spa tracks. Good for serious aches and tension.

blocks.title: Get the most out of your massage
blocks.html: On a day with hard yoga or a full day of riding the motorbike, booking a massage in the late afternoon before heading to the sunset works out perfectly — your body unwinds just in time. Call to book ahead in high season, since slots fill up fast.

blocks.text: The best sunset spots in the area

items: Zen Beach (Sri Thanu) — a popular sunset beach with clear water and white sand, plus a live drum circle in the evening starting around 17:30. Full wellness-community vibe, and free.
Amsterdam Bar (Wok Tum) — a hilltop bar with panoramic views and a pool, open 12:00–01:00, with a drink minimum/entry fee around 100–200 THB. Get there before 16:30 for a good seat.
Hin Kong beach — a quieter beach, good for a calm, uncrowded sunset

blocks.html: If you only have one evening, pick Zen Beach for the full community atmosphere. But if you want a comfortable seat and a wide view, Amsterdam Bar is the easier option. As for drinking, keep it responsible — and if you're riding back at night, go extra slow, because the island roads are dark with plenty of curves and hills.

items: Motorbike — the island roads have several steep hills, so if you're not confident riding, a songthaew or taxi beats forcing it. Always wear a helmet, and photograph the bike's condition when you pick it up to avoid inflated damage claims.
The sea — check the flags and the waves before you swim; the surf gets strong in monsoon season, so don't go in alone in the dark evening.
Valuables — the beach and bars get crowded in the evening, so keep a close eye on your bag, phone, and passport.
Drink responsibly — the beach scene involves drinking, so know your limit, don't accept drinks from strangers, and don't ride after drinking.
Accommodation — avoid Full Moon week if you want it quiet; room prices spike and fill fast then, so book ahead.

faq.q: Where should I stay on Koh Phangan for a wellness trip?
faq.a: Stay on the west side around Sri Thanu–Hin Kong, the wellness area that gathers yoga studios, vegan cafes, massage shops, and sunset beaches within a few kilometers. Travel is short and it's well away from the Haad Rin party noise.

faq.q: How much does a drop-in yoga class cost on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Drop-in single classes run about 250–400 THB each — for example, Orion Healing around 300–400 THB and Samma Karuna around 250–350 THB. No long course required; you can walk in to check the schedule or book ahead.

faq.q: Is it easy to find vegan food on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Very easy, especially around Sri Thanu, where most spots clearly label dishes vegan, raw, or gluten-free. Popular ones include Eat.Co, Street Vegan, Pure Vegan Heaven, and Karma Kafe.

faq.q: Where's a good place to watch the sunset on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: The west side of the island catches a beautiful sunset. The most popular spots are Zen Beach in Sri Thanu, with its evening live drum circle, and Amsterdam Bar on the hill at Wok Tum, with panoramic views and comfortable seating.

faq.q: Should I avoid the Full Moon period if I'm here for wellness?
faq.a: If you want quiet and real rest, avoid the week of the Full Moon Party — room prices spike, places fill fast, and the island gets busier than usual. Book ahead and stay on the Sri Thanu–Hin Kong side for a calmer time.
